chores.title: Edit + delete "I owe {partner}" debts on the settlement page
chores.description: Partner-debt entries (Expense{paidBy:'gf'}) can be created from the settlement page but never edited, and only deleted from the expenses list. They should be editable + deletable on the settlement page, where they belong. Prereq for BUG-1's 'route to settlement to edit' flow.
chores.plan: New updatePartnerDebt action (mirror addPartnerDebt + IDOR-safe updateForUser; preserve paidBy:'gf'/cardId:null/isShared:false/yourPercentage:1/actualExpenditure=amount/no subcategory). PartnerDebtForm gains an edit mode (optional debt prop, prefill via getExpenseForEdit, 'Save changes'). New client SettlementJournalInteractive adds edit + delete (reuse deleteExpense) dialogs on partner_debt rows; router.refresh after. Out of scope: transfers/funded-card/your_expense rows, card-payment editing, all expenses-screen changes (that's BUG-1).

chores.title: Decouple partner money from cards — drop the funded-card-payment flag
chores.description: The 'card payment funded by Brenda' flag encodes two real events as one and spawned the edge cases you hit (money-in vs money-in-then-card vs kept-as-cash). Per the model, money from Brenda is just money in; a card payment is just a card payment; they're never coupled.
chores.plan: Foundation (depends on CHORE-4). (1) Remove Movement.fundedByPartner + the 'funded_card_payment' settlement journal kind. (2) Money-from-Brenda = a plain gf_received transfer-in; a card payment = a plain card_payment — two independent events. (3) settlement.service: moneyPartnerPaidYou = Σ gf_received only (drop the fundedByPartner term from the sum). (4) Simplify the settlement help / info-icon copy now that the edge cases are gone. (5) Prod data migration: existing fundedByPartner card payments → split into a gf_received (money in) + a plain card_payment (reviewed SQL on real data).

chores.title: "I owe {partner}" becomes settlement-only — not an expense (reverses ADR-0018)
chores.description: Today 'I owe Brenda' is stored as Expense{paidBy:'gf'}, so it pollutes the expenses list, categories, budget, and spend-by-card (that's BUG-1's phantom Cash). Per the agreed cash-basis model, a thing she fronted is HER spending and only a debt to you — it must live ONLY in settlement, never in your expenses/consumption. Foundation of the money-model rework.
chores.plan: Reverses ADR-0018 — write the superseding ADR + short spec first (docs/decisions is protected: get sign-off). Then: (1) store the debt as a Movement (new type 'gf_fronted' — she fronted, you owe; amount/date/note, no card) instead of an Expense; addPartnerDebt/updatePartnerDebt write the Movement. (2) settlement.service: yourDebtToPartner = Σ gf_fronted movements (was Σ actualExpenditure of paidBy:'gf'); the journal 'partner_debt' kind reads from movements; re-point CHORE-1's edit/delete onto the movement. (3) Drop paidBy:'gf' from every read — expenses list, dashboard categories/radar/buckets, getCardSpends (phantom gone for free); deprecate Expense.paidBy (all 'you'). (4) Prod data migration: convert existing paidBy:'gf' expenses → gf_fronted movements (real data — Neon MCP survey + reviewed SQL, careful). Retires BUG-1 and the whole 'debt shows as an expense' confusion.

chores.title: Edit + delete money movements (card payments + transfers), with optional note
chores.description: Card payments and settlement transfers are delete-only (delete + re-add), and transfers can't be edited at all — surfaced when a $350 payment was logged as $320 with no way to fix it. Make both editable + deletable, mirroring CHORE-1's settlement-debt edit, and give transfers an optional note. Least urgent of the rework.
chores.plan: New updateMovement action (IDOR-safe, scoped by userId). Edit mode on the movement forms (card-payment form + transfer form); optional free-text note on transfers ('what it was toward' — a label, never a budget category). Reuse CHORE-1's dialog pattern in the settlement journal + the expenses feed. Depends on CHORE-3 (final transfer shape after the funded-card flag is gone).

chores.title: Settings foundation — configurable partner behind an opt-in sharing toggle
chores.description: Make the app usable by anyone: partner identity becomes per-user data behind an opt-in 'I share expenses' toggle, instead of the hardcoded PARTNER_NAME='Brenda' constant (used in 13 files). Foundation of CHORE-6 (spec 0006) — the Settings page and the shared/solo split both build on this flag. The Settings page is currently an empty stub.
chores.plan: Kicks off with an ADR (partner-as-Settings + opt-in sharing mode; docs/decisions is protected — sign-off first). (1) Schema: Settings +sharesExpenses(Boolean, default false) +partnerName(String?); defaultSharePercentage already exists. (2) A getSettings(userId) accessor as the single source; remove the PARTNER_NAME constant and thread the name down as data (no component imports a partner constant). (3) Settings page shell (server component reads Settings) + the Expense-split-rule block: an 'I share expenses' toggle that reveals + requires partner name and your share % when on. Persist via an IDOR-safe server action (name required when toggle on). (4) Owner-account migration: sharesExpenses=true, partnerName='Brenda' (no record rewrites). BUG-2 rider: the same manual owner prod-migration trip also re-seeds prod Category.color (gray→per-slug) and FK-safely deletes the retired Amex Gold card — documented in docs/operations/owner-shared-mode-migration.md, no app code. Tests: action validation, accessor, form both modes. Out of scope: the gating sweep (6.b), card management (6.c), and the deferred mock sections (Account/Preferences/Privacy/Export/theme).

chores.title: Solo mode — hide the shared-expense + settlement machinery when sharing is off
chores.description: With the sharesExpenses flag in place (CHORE-6.a), a solo user must see a plain expense tracker: no split control, no settlement, no partner anywhere. Today that machinery is always on. Depends on CHORE-6.a.
chores.plan: When sharesExpenses=false, hide/guard: (1) the shared/% control in components/expense/ExpenseForm.tsx (expenses save isShared:false, yourPercentage:1, actualExpenditure=amount); (2) the Settlement route + its link in components/nav/AppNav.tsx, plus a server-side route guard (solo user hitting the URL → redirect); (3) the partner items in the Add menu (components/expense/AddExpenseButton.tsx → gf_received/gf_paid/gf_fronted actions); (4) partner widgets on the dashboard. Shared mode renders exactly as today. Tests: each surface in both modes; route guard. Depends on CHORE-6.a.

chores.title: Card management — add / rename / recolor / archive cards in Settings
chores.description: Cards are seeded only; there is no way to add, rename, recolor, or remove one from the app. Add card management to the Settings page. Delete is unsafe (cards are referenced by Expense[] and Movement[]), so removal is soft-archive. Depends on CHORE-6.a (the Settings page shell).
chores.plan: Full card vertical slice (none exists today). (1) Schema: Card +archivedAt(DateTime?). (2) lib/palette.ts: shared named palette (seeded colours + extras) — ends the seed↔login-page hex drift; seed + login import it. (3) lib/schemas/card.ts: Zod (name 1–40, type credit|debit|cash, color validated #RRGGBB — swatch OR custom hex). (4) lib/repositories/card.repository.ts: listActive (archivedAt:null, pickers), listForSettings (all), create, updateForUser, archiveForUser, deleteForUser (IDOR-safe where:{id,userId}; delete uses deleteMany + re-checks Expense/Movement refs, refuses if any). (5) app/_actions/card/{add,update,archive,delete}.ts mirroring save-split-rule (Zod→auth→repo→ActionResult; codes validation|unauthenticated|has_references|not_found|limit_reached|duplicate_name|db_error). (6) Settings Cards section (components/settings/CardsForm.tsx) replaces the coming-soon chip: list + Add form + per-card edit (rename/recolor swatch+hex) + Archive(used)/Delete(unused). (7) Picker reads (expenses/page, dashboard/page) filter archivedAt:null; history reads unfiltered. Rules: Cash fully locked (no edit/archive/delete); archive used / hard-delete unused; unique active name per user (case-insensitive); cap 10 active (MAX_ACTIVE_CARDS); no unarchive. Deferred to CHORE-9: outstanding-balance warn/block on archive. Tests: CRUD actions, validation, IDOR scoping, delete-refuses-when-referenced, hex validation, cap + duplicate-name, archive hides-from-picker-keeps-history, palette module, CardsForm both states. Depends on CHORE-6.a. Full design: docs/specs/0006-settings-standalone-shared-modes.md §6.

chores.title: Toggle dashboard categories between my-share and total spend
chores.description: CANCELLED (2026-07-22): shared-only feature — the toggle is inert in solo mode (a solo user's share IS the total), and the expected prod user base is solo, so the value-to-effort is low. Revisit only if a shared-mode user actually asks for it. Original intent: The dashboard Categories cards + 'Where the money went' show only your share (actualExpenditure, the 68% slice). Add a control to flip them to the full charged amount (ignoring the split) — e.g. Transport shows $2,000 total, not just your part. Aligns with CHORE-6 / spec 0006: in solo mode a user's share IS the total, so the category displays must already support a total basis; build this so the two dovetail (a shared user toggles; a solo user is effectively always 'total').
chores.plan: Scope TBD at build time (decide with the user): a segmented 'My share ⇄ Total' control on the dashboard. Thread both sums per category from the dashboard data (amount-sum + actualExpenditure-sum) so the toggle is a pure client re-scope of the Categories cards + 'Where the money went'. Open question: whether the 50/25/25 buckets + 'Income vs spent' also re-scope (they encode budget-against-your-income, so likely stay my-share). Coordinate with CHORE-6.a/.b (sharesExpenses flag) so solo mode reuses the total-basis path rather than duplicating it.

chores.title: Per-user categories, subcategories, and budgets (multi-tenancy foundation)
chores.description: Category, Subcategory, and CategoryBudget are global (no userId) — one shared config for the whole DB. With public signup (8.d) every user would share the same category set, colors, and monthly budgets; one user editing a budget changes it for everyone. Expenses ARE userId-scoped, so spend stays private, but the scaffolding leaks. Make categories/subcategories/budgets per-user before any signup. Reverses ADR-0016 (budgets deliberately global for the single-user app). Foundation for CHORE-8.b–8.e.
chores.plan: Kicks off with a superseding ADR (reverses ADR-0016; docs/decisions is protected — sign-off first). (1) Schema: +userId on Category, Subcategory, CategoryBudget (relations to User); change CategoryBudget @@unique([categoryId,month]) -> @@unique([userId,categoryId,month]). (2) Owner data migration: backfill userId = owner on all existing Category/Subcategory/CategoryBudget rows so nothing orphans; dev via prisma migrate, PROD via a documented reviewed-SQL runbook (mirror spec 0005's careful-real-data approach — Neon MCP survey before/after). (3) Scope every category/budget read + write by userId: dashboard.repository (getCategorySpends/getCategoryBreakdown), category.repository, category-budget.repository, the set-budget action, seed. (4) Tests: per-user isolation (user A's budget/color invisible to B), userId scoping on every read/write, migration correctness. Depends on nothing new; blocks 8.b/8.c/8.d/8.e.

chores.title: New-user starter kit — default categories/subcategories/cards/settings
chores.description: A single provisioning routine that seeds a fresh account's starting data so a new user lands in a working, private tracker. Shared by the owner seed AND signup (8.d) so the two never drift. Depends on CHORE-8.a (per-user categories).
chores.plan: (1) A provisionNewUser(userId) domain/service routine that seeds, all userId-scoped: the default 13 categories + subcategories (the frozen reference in domain-reference.md), a default Cash card (REQUIRED — Cash is un-addable via the UI since 6.c) plus optional generic Credit + Debit starters, and a default Solo Settings row (sharesExpenses=false). (2) Refactor prisma/seed.ts to provision the owner via the same routine (DRY). (3) Tests: a freshly provisioned user has the full default set, isolated from other users; seed still works. Depends on 8.a.

chores.title: Per-user category management in Settings
chores.description: Now that categories are per-user (8.a), give users a Settings 'Categories' section to manage them — mirroring the Cards section from 6.c. Rename / recolor / add / set monthly budget / archive. Makes the seeded default set adjustable per account.
chores.plan: Mirror the CHORE-6.c card vertical slice for Category: Zod schema, IDOR-safe userId-scoped CRUD actions, a Settings Categories section (client form), reads. Decide exact ops at pickup (rename/recolor/add/set-budget/archive; delete only if unused, else archive — categories are referenced by Expense[]). Coordinates with the existing inline dashboard budget editing (set-budget) so they share the same per-user path. Depends on 8.a.

chores.title: Public signup, capped to a configurable max users in PROD
chores.description: Add a real signup page, bounded: PROD accepts at most N users (default 10) so onboarding stays small and controlled. Reverses the 'no signup' deferral in spec 0006 §8. A new account is provisioned via the 8.b starter kit so it lands in a clean, private Solo tracker. Depends on 8.a + 8.b.
chores.plan: (1) Signup page (app/(auth)/signup, mirror the login page/form -> server action pattern) + public server action: email + password + display name (Zod; password strength), bcrypt.hash(pw,10) like the seed, create User then provisionNewUser (8.b). Replace the SignUpComingSoon placeholder on the login page with a real link. (2) User cap: MAX_USERS env var (default 10) checked BEFORE create — db.user.count vs cap, reject at-cap with a clear 'signups are currently full' message; document in .env.example + coding-conventions.md. (3) After signup, sign the user in (auto) and route to onboarding (8.e). (4) Empty-state: dashboard shows a 'set your income' nudge when a user has no income (not a dead 0/0/0). (5) Update spec 0006 §8. Tests: happy path, duplicate-email reject, at-cap boundary (N-1 ok, N rejected), validation, password hashed (never plain). Out of scope: email verification, password reset, OAuth, rate-limiting beyond the cap. Depends on 8.a + 8.b.

chores.title: Signup onboarding wizard
chores.description: After a user signs up (8.d), walk them through a short multi-step onboarding (modal/wizard) to set up their account instead of dropping them on an empty dashboard. Built against a user-provided Claude design reference.
chores.plan: A multi-step wizard shown on first sign-in: welcome -> display name + fixed monthly income -> pick/confirm a card (from the starter kit) -> 'do you share expenses?' toggle (+ partner name + your % when on) -> budget rule (show the default 50/25/25 as a starting point) -> done. Persists via the existing settings / income / card paths (no new money model). Steps + visuals finalized against the shared design. Depends on 8.d (a just-signed-up user) + 8.a/8.b. Out of scope: re-running the wizard later (Settings already covers edits).

chores.title: Per-card outstanding balance
chores.description: Show the current outstanding balance per card — the stat deferred since ADR-0018's era, refreshed for the cash-basis money model. Read-model + display only, no new capture (expenses already carry cardId; card payments are Movement{type:'card_payment', cardId}). Converted from the old backlog slice 2.13 (PR #46, closed) because it's feedback-driven and interlocks with card management (CHORE-6.c). Logging-completeness-bound: accurate only if every charge is logged — label it 'based on logged expenses', not the bank statement.
chores.plan: (1) Read-model, userId-scoped, behind the repository (no db in components): outstanding(card) = Sum of expense.amount charged to that card MINUS Sum of movement.amount where type='card_payment' and cardId matches. Use expense.amount (the FULL charge to the card) — NOT actualExpenditure: the card was charged the full amount regardless of any expense split; card balance is source-agnostic (spec 0005 §3). (2) Surface it on the dashboard 'Spend by card' area or a dedicated per-card view (exact surface: brainstorm on pickup); label 'based on logged expenses'. (3) CHORE-6.c interaction (careful): an archived card can still carry a nonzero outstanding balance, so this display MUST still show archived cards whose balance != 0 (never hide a card you still owe on) — pickers stay archived-filtered, this display does not. Coordinate with 6.c so archiving a card with a nonzero outstanding warns/blocks. Depends on CHORE-6.c. Tests: outstanding math (charges - payments; uses amount, ignores split), userId scoping, archived-but-nonzero card still shown, zero-balance card. Out of scope: reconciling against a real bank statement, editing card balances directly.

chores.title: Settlement cycles and the payment-is-the-expense inversion (slices E' and F)
chores.description: The whole settlement and partner-money story, split across two PRs that must merge in order. Registered late: this work ran for two sessions with no roadmap entry at all, so the SessionStart hooks reported 'no slice' and a cold agent reading the roadmap would have seen nothing in flight. The model: what he owes the partner lives in settlement only — absent from both feeds, every bucket, every category — and the payment he sends her is the Expense that counts in the budget. Settlements became cycles, with membership by entry time in a half-open window (previousMarker, marker]. Funding source (income | savings | reimbursed) marks which month's money paid for a row; only income reaches the 50/25/25 budget, and a savings-funded transfer still counts in the settlement balance.
chores.plan: PR #74 (slice E', branch feat/settlement-cycles): the inversion, settlement cycles, the month switcher, and rounding fixed at the cause. PR #73 (branch feat/funding-source-expenses): funding source on expenses and on transfers to the partner. MERGE ORDER IS #74 THEN #73 — #73 builds on the settlement read #74 restructured, and #74 carries spec 0007 to main (it is absent from #73's tree, so ADR-0023 cites a spec not in its own branch). Both PRs are SCHEMA ONLY: vercel.json runs 'prisma migrate deploy' on every production build, so a merge is an unreviewed production data migration — every data statement was pulled out and deferred to CHORE-12. Slice F still owes the removal of the cross-ledger Total figure (spec 0007 §6b assigns it to slice F; it survives in lib/domain/movement.ts until then). Decisions: ADR-0024 (the payment is the expense) and ADR-0023 (funding source), both signed off 2026-09-15. After #74 merges, delete the superseded branch feat/fronted-debt-as-expense — it carries a divergent copy of spec 0007.

chores.title: Settlement marker mirror + the deferred production data migration
chores.description: The two halves of what CHORE-11 deliberately left undone, which must ship together. HALF 1, a known gap shipped in #74: closedAt lives only on Movement, but after the inversion a payment to the partner is an Expense — so a cycle squared only by paying the partner cannot be closed at all, which is the main flow. #74 contains this by returning a real no_marker error instead of reporting a success it did not achieve. HALF 2: the production data conversion pulled out of #74 and #73. They cannot be separated, because a gf_paid movement carrying closedAt has nowhere to put that marker until half 1 lands.
chores.plan: Branch off feat/settlement-cycles, not main. Depends on CHORE-11 merging first. (1) Expense.closedAt mirroring Movement.closedAt, with the same constraint shape, and every marker read becoming a union of both tables — find them all. (2) The data conversion, following spec 0005 §6: pre-flight counts, one transaction, idempotent, and a per-user settlement-balance compare before and after that must match to the cent. It also flips the subcategory rename ('Purchases made by girlfriend' -> 'Covered for me'), which #74 deliberately reverted: rename the ROWS by id first, then PARTNER_PAYMENT_SUBCATEGORY_NAME and prisma/seed.ts together, never separately — the seed matches subcategories by name, so a half-done rename creates a duplicate on the next re-seed. (3) HARD REQUIREMENT: the conversion MUST reuse the movement's id for the expense it creates. Three places already assume it (withoutConvertedTwins in settlement.service.ts, the twin-dedup in lib/domain/movement.ts, and ADR-0024) and nothing enforces it; new ids would double every transfer in paidToPartner, total and moneyYouPaidPartner. (4) Prefer additive — do not delete a converted movement unless you can show a read path double-counts it. (5) A read-only survey in docs/operations/ for the owner to run himself; never connect to production. Rollout: survey production, take a Neon restore point, then merge — merging IS the migration. The deferred SQL and the two preserved integration test files are held outside the repo at ~/.claude/harness/tasks/fet-payment-is-the-expense/.

chores.title: One month chooser, shared by every page, that survives navigation
chores.description: RE-CONFIRMED in manual testing after #74 merged: switching sections still drops you back to the current month instead of keeping the one in the query param. The switcher remembers your choice on Settlement only. MonthPicker already writes the shared cookie on every page that renders it; only Settlement reads it back, so Expenses sets the memory and then ignores its own write. The owner also wants the control itself made consistent: the SAME component on every page, with Settlement's 'take me back' affordance being the only page-specific addition. That button needs a background so it reads as a button rather than text, and active verbiage — 'Take me back to the current month' or similar, not a bare label. Ids 10, 11 and 12 are taken by in-flight branches; this is 13 deliberately.
chores.plan: SHIPS WITH CHORE-14, in the same PR and worktree — decided 2026-09-17. Both touch app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx and app/(dashboard)/expenses/page.tsx, so splitting them across two parallel branches guarantees a conflict in exactly the files that already cost a 28-file merge. One PR owns that surface. (1) Make the resolution shared: both pages already accept ?month= and resolve `monthParam ?? now`. Swap that for `await getScopedMonth(monthParam)` (lib/month-scope.server.ts) — one line each in app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx and app/(dashboard)/expenses/page.tsx — and render <MonthPicker month={month} /> on Dashboard, which has none. Precedence stays URL param, then remembered month, then today, so a shared link still pins its month. (2) Make the CONTROL shared: one component used by Dashboard, Expenses and Settlement, with the back-to-current affordance as an optional prop rather than a second implementation. Give that button a real background and active copy. (3) Check the rendered result on all three pages — this is the fault the owner noticed twice, so a browser pass is part of the work, not optional. Tests: a stored month is honoured when no param is present; an explicit param beats the stored month; an invalid param falls back rather than throwing; the choice survives Dashboard → Expenses → Settlement in both directions.

chores.title: Rebuild the expenses chin as a nested, colour-coded breakdown with a chart
chores.description: The footer grew to six flat lines across PRs #73 and #74 and stopped reading as one idea. Owner, looking at a real September: 'it is confusing just reading it, it is too much information and I think we could organize it better.' He gave the structure he wants, and it is a HIERARCHY, not a list — that is the point, and a flat row per figure is what makes it unreadable: Charged in total (its own pill-shaped colour), then What I really spent, with a nested line for how much of that came from savings, a nested line for how much went to the partner, and under THAT a line for how much of the partner payment came from savings. He also wants colour, and — because even nested this is a lot on one bar — the chin clickable to open a modal with a chart, probably a pie. BUG-5 is the same defect from the data side and is fixed here: a savings-funded payment currently appears in NO line at all, because paidToPartner counts income-funded rows only and notFromIncomeTransfers holds movements only. Nesting it under 'What I really spent → paid to partner → from savings' is exactly where he expects it.
chores.plan: THE DESIGN IS docs/designs-screens/Summary breakdown modal.html — read it before planning anything; it supersedes the four-figure sketch this chore originally carried. It covers the desktop modal, the mobile full-screen sheet, and BOTH strips that open it (Dashboard right-rail footer, Expenses sticky footer bar), and its framing is 'two pots': this month's income versus savings. Its figures are real September 2026 values and were verified against the running app — Charged 36,046.51, my income 19,450.82, my savings 11,700.00, paid to Brenda 24,466.23, of that 1,000.00 from savings — so most of the modal re-organises figures that already exist rather than inventing maths. DECIDED 2026-09-17 — the owner chose OPTION A, gross. The design's 'Total out of this month's income' subtracted what the partner paid you from consumption. Do NOT build it that way. 'What I really spent' is already YOUR SHARE only — verified on September: 36,046.51 charged minus 11,700.00 savings minus 4,895.69 her share equals 19,450.82 — so her share was never in it, and subtracting her reimbursement removes money that was already excluded. That is a double subtraction, not merely a ledger-rule question. Build the row GROSS: card spend from income plus paid to partner from income, no netting. The net-with-partner figure belongs on the SETTLEMENT page, where cash in and cash out are meant to meet; the design's own 'Net with Brenda' section is the right home for it and stays out of this chin. WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW (everything else exists): per-transfer rows with dates ('Paid you — 30 sep'), the partner's outstanding 32% on shared expenses, and the 'what she put in' donut — all settlement-side figures the chin has never read. BUILD ORDER: (1) model the hierarchy in computeFeedTotals so each nested figure is a BREAKDOWN of its parent in the TYPE, not in a comment, and add the savings-funded-payment figure BUG-5 needs; (3) build the strips, which are the entry points and the smaller half; (4) build the modal and the donuts — the design draws them inline as SVG, and per docs/designs-screens/README.md that is layout reference only, so use a charting lib or small custom SVG; (5) handle the payment-only edge case where 'What I really spent' and 'Paid to {partner}' print the same number twice — the design's nesting already fixes it by labelling the child. Fold CHORE-19 (the unsettled-balance reminder) into the same pass rather than touching this chin twice. Tests: each figure against mixed-funding fixtures; a page-level assertion that no two rows state the same money; and the loop-every-field guard from the #73 review asserting no field equals the forbidden cross-ledger sum — EXEMPTING the partner-payment figures, which legitimately sum payment-expenses with their unconverted legacy movements under the spec 0007 §6a carve-out added 2026-09-17. FIRST TASK, inherited from BUG-5: 'Not from this month's income' and 'Paid to {partner} from savings' currently render as siblings with identical styling, and on the owner's October data both print $530 — stacked, they read as $1,060 of savings spent. The second is partly a subset of the first. Nest it or relabel it 'of which paid to {partner}'; the hierarchy this chore builds is exactly the fix.

chores.title: Thread the funding flag through the feed totals, and refuse a frozen row at the edit read
chores.description: Two follow-ups the #73 and #74 review rounds deliberately deferred, grouped because both are 'a predicate narrower than the read path it mirrors' — the shape that produced six defects across those reviews. (a) computeFeedTotals in lib/domain/movement.ts partitions on the NARROWED fundedFrom, so a stored value outside the enum lands in whatIReallySpent instead of the non-income figure, breaking the cross-screen agreement spec 0007 §2 exists to guarantee. Unreachable through the app because Zod validates writes; reachable via a raw DB edit or a future fourth funding value. (b) getMovementForEdit and getExpenseForEdit prefill a frozen row without refusing, so a stale tab can open a dialog that can only fail on save. Loud and non-corrupting — every write path refuses — but the two reads are symmetric and fixing one alone would repeat the one-surface mistake.
chores.plan: (a) Carry countedInBudget out of expense.repository.ts the way category.repository.ts already does, computed from the RAW column via isBudgetFunded, and thread it through FeedTotalExpense, MonthFeed.tsx and ExpenseListInteractive.tsx plus their fixtures. isBudgetFunded is already exported. Test with an out-of-band value written directly to the database, at the real seam. (b) Have both edit reads return the cycle_closed refusal the write paths return, using the same movesSettlementBalance / movementMovesSettlementBalance predicates, so the read and the write agree by construction. Do both in one slice. Depends on CHORE-11 and the #73 merge, since (a) touches a file both branches rewrote.

chores.title: Clean up after the settlement rework — branches, worktrees and review debt
chores.description: Housekeeping that accumulated across the two settlement sessions. None of it changes behaviour; all of it misleads the next reader if left. The divergent spec copy is the sharpest item: feat/fronted-debt-as-expense carries a docs/specs/0007 about 130 lines apart from the live one, so anyone who opens that branch reads a superseded design as if it were current.

chores.title: Bring the existing code back to the comment bar
chores.description: coding-conventions.md says 'default to no comment' and caps an earned one at 1-3 lines. The codebase does not follow it: 108 files carry 274 comment blocks over the cap, holding 1,996 lines between them. lib/ sits at roughly 24% comment lines. The rule and the code drifted apart long before the settlement rework, and the drift is self-sustaining — agents are told to match the neighbouring file's density, so every new file reproduces the house style and reads as compliant while doing it. The worst offenders: lib/services/settlement/settlement.service.ts (28 blocks, 219 lines), lib/domain/expense.ts (8, 88), lib/repositories/movement.repository.ts (8, 75), lib/domain/movement.ts (6, 75), lib/repositories/expense.repository.ts (8, 73), components/settlement/SettlementJournal.tsx (10, 71). Measured on the CHORE-11 branch, so it includes that work's own comments; the pre-existing share is lower but still most of it.
chores.plan: Do this AFTER CHORE-11 and the #73 merge land, or it conflicts with everything. Not one PR — 108 files is unreviewable. Slice it worst-first by directory, roughly four passes: (1) lib/services and lib/domain, (2) lib/repositories, (3) app/_actions, (4) components. Each pass is its own PR, small enough to read. Method, the one that worked on the two settlement PRs: run a reviewer over the diff with a comments-only lens and have it return a verdict per block — DELETE (restates the code, review narration, reader infers it), SHRINK (with the exact 1-3 line replacement text written out, so the implementer pastes rather than re-judges), or KEEP (only above the cap, and only with a demonstration of what a reader loses if it were cut — 'it explains the design' is not a reason). Then an implementer applies the verdicts verbatim and runs the full gates; comments only, no logic touched, so any test failure means a real edit slipped in. Two lenses beyond size: delete any comment that is now FALSE, since a comment that lies is worse than none; and strip review-provenance tags ('Round 4', 'for two rounds', 'that's how X shipped'), which belong in git history. scripts/check-comment-size.sh warns on newly added over-cap blocks, so this cleanup stops the bleeding rather than being repeated later. Out of scope: tests/ (different density norms) and any comment linking an ADR for a non-obvious decision, which the convention explicitly allows.

chores.title: Show savings-funded spend on the dashboard
chores.description: Owner request from manual testing: 'add a dash graph/category to show how much money I spent with my savings money.' Today the dashboard's 50/25/25 buckets deliberately exclude every savings-funded row (spec 0007 §2 — that money was counted as savings in the month it was earned, so counting it again double-counts), and the only place the figure surfaces is a footnote line under the buckets. So the dashboard answers 'how is this month's income being used' and never answers 'how much of my savings did I spend', which is a question he actually has. The data already exists: getNonIncomeFundedTotal is on dashboard.repository.ts, and CHORE-14 adds the payment-side breakdown.
chores.plan: Brainstorm the surface with the owner before building — he said 'graph/category' without picking one, and the dashboard is dense already. Two candidates: a fourth card beside the three buckets, visually distinct so it never reads as a fourth slice of the 50/25/25 (it is NOT income being allocated), or a segment in 'Where the money went'. Whatever it is, it must state which question it answers, because a savings figure beside three income buckets invites reading it as part of the same 100%. Reuse getNonIncomeFundedTotal rather than adding a query. Show the reimbursed share separately or exclude it — 'spent from savings' and 'refunded' are different events that both land in notFromIncome. Depends on CHORE-14, which defines the breakdown shape. Tests: the figure matches the expenses chin for the same month; a month with no savings-funded row renders nothing rather than a zero.

chores.title: Surface an unsettled balance on the Expenses chin, linking to Settlement
chores.description: Owner request: 'if I owe Brenda money, or she owes me, I should see the button/reminder on the chin on the expenses page, clicking it should take me to the settlement page.' Today the balance lives only on the Settlement page, so the one screen he uses daily gives no sign that money is outstanding — he has to remember to go and look. The dashboard feed already renders an 'All settled' pill linking to /settlement (components/dashboard/MonthFeed.tsx), so the pattern exists and the Expenses chin simply does not carry it.
chores.plan: Reuse the dashboard's settlement pill rather than inventing a second treatment, and state the direction and the amount — 'You owe Brenda $X' / 'Brenda owes you $X' — not a bare 'unsettled', since the direction is the whole point. Settled stays quiet or shows the existing calm state; do not nag when nothing is owed. It is the OPEN cycle's balance, not the selected month's: the balance belongs to a cycle, not a month (spec 0007 §3.5), so viewing March must not imply March's balance. Land it with CHORE-14, which is rebuilding that chin anyway — adding a row now and restructuring it immediately after is two passes over one component. Tests: each direction renders with the right wording and amount; settled renders the calm state; the link targets /settlement; the figure matches the settlement page for the same account.
